title: Frappe versions documents, but the versions are mutable rows and are deletable
content:
Frappe does version documents, which is why this cohort needs a precise argument rather than a general one about audit trails. The versions are mutable rows in the ERP's own tables and they are deletable, so the mechanism that looks like an audit trail is subject to the same write and delete paths as the data it describes.

The proposed position is correspondingly narrow: Powerhouse holds the append-only record of the submitted business event, outside the ERP's own tables. "Outside" is the operative word — the guarantee comes from the record not sharing a lifecycle with the ERP's schema, not from a claim that Frappe records nothing.

For the three German ERPNext partners carrying this finding, all at "1 · start here", the argument has to be made to people who know Frappe's versioning well. Overstating the gap would be immediately falsifiable; stating it as mutability and deletability rather than absence is both accurate and sufficient.
